title: Capability Catalog
description: The Capability state variable: what the assembled system can actually do, as discovered by or for a grantee. This object confers no authority and contains no permission fields by design (Law I: capability does not imply authority). Anything the grantee is permitted to do is stated only in an authority grant (authority-grant.schema.json) that references this catalog; a capability listed here without a matching grant is discoverable but not executable.

schema_version.title: Schema version
schema_version.description: Version of this schema the catalog conforms to.

catalog_id.title: Catalog identifier
catalog_id.description: Stable identifier for this catalog so grants and safety object models can reference it.

grantee.title: Grantee
grantee.description: The agent, role, system, or human whose reachable capabilities this catalog describes.

id.title: Grantee identifier
id.description: Stable identifier of the grantee, matching the grantee id used in authority grants.

type.title: Grantee type
type.description: What kind of component the grantee is.

discovered_at.title: Discovered at
discovered_at.description: When this catalog was last discovered or refreshed. Capability drifts; the timestamp lets reviewers compare it to the authority state.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.description: Each action the grantee could take if it were authorized. Listing an action here says nothing about whether it is allowed.

items.title: Capability
items.description: One discoverable capability of the grantee.

action_class.title: Action class
action_class.description: The class of consequential action this capability falls under, such as READ, WRITE, or TRANSFER. Grants authorize action classes, not individual capabilities.

description.title: Description
description.description: Plain-language statement of what the capability does.

state.title: State
state.description: Latest known state of the capability, using exactly the states a STD-07 capability record carries (STD-07 §3.4). absent: not reachable. configured: present but no check has passed. verified: a check has passed. broken: a check has failed. The distinction is load-bearing: an authority grant that depends on this capability is valid only while the capability's latest record is verified. configured is not enough, and a capability that falls to broken invalidates the grants resting on it until it is verified again.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Tool, API, or integration names through which the capability is reachable.

reversible.title: Reversible
reversible.description: Whether exercising this capability can be undone without unacceptable damage.

discovered_via.title: Discovered via
discovered_via.description: How the capability was discovered, for example tool introspection, integration inventory, or red-team probe.
